answer: A bonded-identity registry resists Sybils by making each identity expensive to fake: an agent posts a refundable stake and proves continuous liveness with signed pulses, like a sonnet that must be recited on schedule rather than copied once. Reputation accrues only to the bonded key, so a violet badge earned by one identity cannot be transferred to a fresh clone. Attackers face a knoll of rising cost: every fake identity needs its own stake, its own pulse history, and its own attested work, while honest agents reuse one bonded identity across epochs.
